key_insight: Correcting systematic biases in binding-affinity datasets (e.g., target/scaffold overlap and measurement artifacts) substantially improves model generalization to new compounds and targets, revealing that prior performance gains were often driven by biased splits rather than true predictive power.
problem_solved: Addresses misleading performance estimates caused by dataset bias and leakage in binding-affinity prediction, which produce overoptimistic models that fail to generalize to novel chemical matter or biological targets.
method: Diagnose dataset biases and overlap (e.g., scaffold/target leakage, measurement heterogeneity) using quantitative analyses.
Apply debiasing actions: curated resplitting or holdout protocols, reweighting/importance-sampling, and controlled retraining to remove shortcuts.
Re-evaluate models under rigorous, unbiased benchmarks to demonstrate improved out-of-distribution generalization.
impact: Provides a practical roadmap for more reliable affinity predictors: better dataset practices and evaluation protocols yield models that transfer to real-world drug-discovery scenarios, reducing wasted experimental follow-up and false confidence in ML results.
